title: Every Dual National Now Cap-Tied to the USMNT Following Concacaf Nations League
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Zach LowyNov 14, 2026Santiago Castañeda has fully committed to playing for the USMNT. / Robin Alam/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesThe U.S. men’s national team closed out the Mauricio Pochettino era in style on Tuesday, with first-half goals from Christian Pulisic and Julian Hall to defeat Haiti 2–0 in Cincinnati in the second leg of the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals. An 8–0 aggregate result confirms the team’s spot in the Concacaf Nations League semifinals.

The first leg in Miami saw various players like Julian Hall, Adri Mehmeti and Justin Ellis commit their international future to the USMNT, and the second leg did not disappoint in this regard either, with Pochettino locking down every possible player who could have switched nationalities.
Here is every dual (or tri) national that sealed their future with the Stars and Stripes.

The USMNT has discovered a gem in Julian Hall.  / JC Ruiz/Getty ImagesJulian Hall took Major League Soccer by storm this season as Red Bull New York’s starting center forward, so it’s no surprise that both the U.S. and Poland have been vying for his hand. However, it was the former who gave the 18-year-old his senior debut. Last month, Hall became just the third player in federation history to score in each of his first three USMNT appearances, before being held scoreless against Canada.

FIFA’s rules regarding dual nationals dictate that once a player under the age of 21 plays more than three competitive international matches for a nation—including at least one official competition—then they are locked into representing that country.

But while Hall had met the minimum threshold of total appearances last camp (four), he still hadn’t played in a competitive setting, meaning he wasn’t officially cap-tied. That changed on Saturday when he started up top in the Concacaf competition. Poland will now have to look elsewhere for a long-term replacement for 38-year-old Robert Lewandowski in attack.

Mathis Albert has permanently committed to playing for the USMNT. / JC Ruiz/Getty ImagesHe has only played two club matches this season, and he doesn’t turn 18 for another six months, but Mathis Albert is already emerging as an important figure in the USMNT’s attack.

After playing in all four friendlies in the previous window and even scoring against Chile, Albert made his competitive debut against Haiti on Saturday after replacing Pulisic in the 81st minute. No matter what, he is now permanently cap-tied and will not be able to switch international allegiances to France or Germany.

Adri Mehmeti has enjoyed a breakout year for club and country. / Leonardo Fernandez/USSF/Getty ImagesAnother player who became permanently cap-tied in Miami was Adri Mehmeti. The 17-year-old had played against Peru, Chile and Canada in the previous window, and by making his fourth appearance in a competitive setting, he is now tied to the USMNT. Having previously represented Albania at the U-15 level, he is now fully committed to representing the Stars and Stripes.

Justin Ellis is officially locked in with the USMNT. / Omar Vega/Getty ImagesWith the U.S. cruising to a 6–0 win, Pochettino brought on Justin Ellis for his fourth international appearance and permanently cap-tied the 19-year-old striker. It was a damning blow for Uruguay manager Diego Forlán, who traveled to Orlando in September to watch him play and attempt to poach him for La Celeste.

Diego Kochen is challenging Matt Freese for the USMNT's starting position between the sticks. / Leonardo Fernandez/USSF/Getty ImagesPochettino spent the majority of his USMNT tenure going with Matt Freese in goal, but he ended his journey with a new face in between the sticks: Diego Kochen. After coming off the bench against Peru and starting against Mexico last month, Kochen has laid down the gauntlet in his second consecutive international window.
Whereas the September-October window saw Pochettino start four different goalkeepers, the manager gave Kochen the nod ahead of Brian Schwake and Freese for both legs in November.

He only just turned 20, but Kochen is already proving why he could be the long-term answer in goal. And by playing in both matches against Haiti, he is now unable to switch allegiances to Peru or Venezuela.

He's only 19, but Neil Pierre is towering above the opposition. / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty ImagesHaiti’s first trip to the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals ended in tears, and to make matters even worse, Les Grenadiers have missed out on one of their most prized dual nationals: Neil Pierre.

Born and raised in Pennsylvania to Haitian parents, Pierre has enjoyed a breakout 2026 with the Philadelphia Union, and it’s no surprise that Pochettino was intrigued by his abilities. After replacing Chris Richards at halftime in the second leg, he is now fully committed to the USMNT.

Cavan Sullivan is proving why he is one of the best young talents in North America. / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty ImagesPierre isn’t the only Philadelphia Union academy graduate who became cap-tied on Tuesday.  Previously eligible to represent Germany and Bangladesh, Cavan Sullivan has now permanently committed to playing for the USMNT after replacing Pulisic in the 65th minute.

Sullivan has emerged as one of the best players in MLS this season at 17 years old, and it’s no surprise that he’s already featuring prominently for the Stars and Stripes. After becoming the youngest goal scorer in USMNT history against Mexico, Sullivan looks set to continue his pivotal role under the new team manager.
